main_text.p: bet quo reclinet caput : habetur pro fabro : pro Marc.6. dæmoniaco : pro helluone : pro impostore: est Ioh.8.[?] lapis reprobatus : equitat super asina, &c. Matth. 11.
Obiectio. Cantic.1. Pulcher es dilecte mi: & Ni-Matth.27. cephorus formam ejus describit non inelegan-Matth.21.tem : ὡραῖος τῷ ὄψιν, &c.

Resp. Non corporis & personæ, sed conditio-nis & Regni species contemta intelligitur: Sed coram mundo: ideo dicit: Coram eo: nempe in-fideli populo Iudaico: quia mundus imaginatur sibi Messiam magnificum, terrenum: fastidit vero Christi humilitatem & mortem.
Transseatur[?] ad hujus narrationem, & ostenda-tur mirus circumstantiarum consensus cum hi-storia.

III. Ex defectione populi mei plaga ei. Per defectionem intelligit apostasiam a Deo, impietatem, proditionem: Per populum suum, Iudæos: sicut Dan.9. Super populum tuum, h. e, ex quo tu natus, cujus tu es civis, propheta, &c. Ergo impietate & scelere Iudæorum prodetur, capietur & trucidabitur. Zach.9. Venditus est 30. argenteis.
Evangelistæ: Tempore Christi regnabat apostasia: Pharisæi insidiantur Christo: pacisc[?]un-tur cum Iuda[?]: proditur 30. argenteis, capitur in horto[?], ut latro, &c.

IV. Per coarctationem & judicium sublatus est. Alii. De angustia & judicio: quasi de resurrectio-ne loquatur Propheta, &c. Sed modus poenæ si-gnificatur: sistendum judicio: accusandum, con-spuendum, colaphis, contumeliis coarctandum: ac iudicis sententia damnandum, &c. Iel[?]. 50. v.6:

page.notes: Lower part of the page is faded and partly obscured by show-through: the lines "horto, ut latro" and "Iuda" are doubtful, as is "Ioh.8." (marginal reference, possibly Ioh. 8). "Transseatur" has a doubtful long-s ligature. "pacisc[?]untur" is a doubtful reading of the word split at the line end. "Iel." may be Ier. The Greek "ὡραῖος τῷ ὄψιν" is doubtful. The text "speciem contemta" and "species" in the Resp. paragraph follow the scan as far as legible.
